question: An enzyme inhibitor that reduces the Vm and Km of an enzyme in the same proportion is an inhibitor of type:
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Inhibitor binds to the enzyme -> Reduces Vm and Km in the same proportion -> Not competitive inhibitor -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Inhibitor binds to a site other than the active site -> Alters enzyme kinetics without affecting substrate binding -> Mixed inhibitor -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Inhibitor binds to the enzyme-substrate complex -> Reduces the enzyme's ability to catalyze the reaction -> Acompetitive inhibitor -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Inhibitor competes with the substrate for the active site -> Reduces the enzyme's affinity for the substrate -> Competitive inhibitor -> 95%
analysis: An enzyme inhibitor that reduces the Vm and Km of an enzyme in the same proportion is indicative of a competitive inhibitor. Competitive inhibitors bind to the active site of the enzyme, competing with the substrate. This results in an increase in Km (substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity) and a decrease in Vm (maximal reaction velocity) as the inhibitor competes with the substrate for binding to the enzyme.
